takeaway: Keloids extend beyond the wound edges and usually do not settle; hypertrophic scars stay within the wound and usually settle within 18 months.

question.text: Regarding wound healing on the skin, all of the following statements are true EXCEPT which one?
question.say: Regarding wound healing on the skin, all of the following statements are true, except which one?

answer.text: Not true: a keloid scar usually settles spontaneously in up to 18 months.

lines.text: Here the question is an except: we are hunting the false statement.
A wound closed surgically heals by primary intention. True.
In secondary intention the wound is left open, and epithelium grows in from the edges towards the centre. True.
A hypertrophic scar does not extend beyond the wound edges, and usually settles within eighteen months. True.
But a keloid has excessive collagen and fibroblasts, extends beyond the wound, and usually does not settle.
So the false statement is that a keloid usually settles spontaneously.
lines.say: (clears throat) So the false statement is that a keloid usually settles spontaneously.
